title: Responder Training Lab Playbook and Incident Command Simulator
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook defines a repeatable training program and an automated incident command simulator tailored to Redwood Inference production signals. The goal is to accelerate responder proficiency, validate runbooks, and reduce time-to-recovery for common failure classes (serving latency regressions, KV cache loss, GPU pool saturations, and cross-region network blips).

Audience
- Primary: on-call engineers, bridge operators, incident commanders, SRE mentors.
- Secondary: product liaisons, support leads, and platform engineering.

Goals
- Verify runbook correctness for top 5 incident classes.
- Reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) by 30% and mean time to mitigate (MTTM) by 25% within 3 quarters.
- Ensure all on-call engineers complete at least 2 simulated incidents per quarter.

Roles and responsibilities (during simulation)
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates triage, approves mitigation steps.
- Bridge Operator: runs diagnostics, executes safe remediation commands.
- Service Owner (SME): interprets telemetry and authorizes config changes.
- Communications Lead: drafts customer and internal updates.
- Observer/Proctor: scores the run and records learning notes.

Simulation cadence and format
1) Frequency: weekly 60–90 minute labs led by SRE proctors; quarterly full-cadence war rooms (2–4 hours).
2) Team size: 3–6 active responders + 1 proctor + 1 communications lead.
3) Environment: isolated staging namespace that mirrors production telemetry and can inject the following fault types: latency spike, error spike, KV cache eviction, GPU host flapping, and inter-region packet loss.
4) Safety: simulator uses non-prod namespaces and circuit breakers; no customer data is used.

Scoring rubric (proctor checklist)
- Detection: Alert acknowledged within target window (target = 3 minutes).
- Triage: Correctly classified incident class and SLO impact within 10 minutes.
- Containment: Implemented safe throttles/fallbacks within 20 minutes.
- Communication: Internal and customer templates used, with clear ETA and impact statement.
- Recovery: Service restored to baseline or acceptable degraded mode with rollback plan.
- After-action: Postmortem draft created with timeline and at least two actionable mitigation items.

Incident lifecycle for simulator scenarios (step-by-step)
1) Alerting and first response\   - Observe incoming alert and verify anomalous signal via telemetry dashboards (per-route latency, error-rate, capacity).\   - IC confirms scope: region(s), customer subsets, models impacted.\   - If alert is false positive, document metrics and close with a note.
2) Triage and containment\   - Run standard diagnostic checklist: 
     - Check service health endpoints: curl -fsS https://platform-monitoring/_health || true\     - Query per-route P95: curl -s 'https://metrics/api?series=route_latency.p95&route=...'
     - Inspect queue depths, backpressure, GPU utilization (nvidia-smi wrapper): /opt/redwood/bin/gpu-util.sh --list
   - Apply containment: scale up worker pool, enable degraded model variant, or enable rate-limiting exemptions. Prefer non-destructive steps first.
3) Mitigation and recovery\   - Work with service owner to apply a controlled mitigation (examples below).\   - Validate recovery by observing: request success rate >98% and P95 latency within SLO for 10 continuous minutes.\   - If mitigation fails, escalate to cross-team bridge and consider traffic diversion or rollback.
4) Customer communications\   - Communications lead posts an initial internal incident note within 10 minutes and crafts customer-facing status messages (templates below).
5) Post-incident review\   - IC assigns a postmortem owner and ensures the postmortem is published within 72 hours.

Standard mitigation examples (safe-first)
- GPU pool saturation\   - Symptoms: P95 latency > 2x baseline, queue depth rising, GPU mem < 10% free on average.\   - Containment steps:\     1. Reduce new request admission via token bucket throttle: curl -X POST $ADMIN/policies/throttle -d '{"service":"generation","rate":0.6}'\     2. Shift non-critical traffic to cheaper/quantized model variants via routing policy: /admin/routing/patch --json '{"route":"/generate","fallback":"gptq-small:v2"}'\     3. Add capacity by scaling the dedicated pool (if allowed): terraform apply -var='add_gpu=2' -target=module.gpu_pool\   - Validation: p95 returns to <300ms and failures drop below 0.5% within 15 minutes.

- KV cache mass eviction\   - Symptoms: sudden latency increase for short requests, spike in model recompute tokens.\   - Containment steps:\     1. Enable prefix caching fallback for hot prefixes: /admin/cache/fallback --set hot_prefix=true\     2. Temporarily raise small-request weight in load balancer to prioritize low-latency paths.\     3. Restart the cache service with preserved checkpoint: systemctl restart kv-cache && /opt/redwood/bin/cache-restore --checkpoint=/checkpoints/latest\   - Validation: cache hit rate >80% and p95 drops toward baseline in 10–20 minutes.

- Cross-region networking blip\   - Symptoms: increased egress errors to secondary region, global routing jitter.\   - Containment steps:\     1. Enable regional failover for critical routes: /admin/route/failover --region=us-east-1\     2. Remove non-essential cross-region traffic and reduce replication window.\     3. Open bridge with network team and coordinate BGP checks.\   - Validation: degraded endpoints return to local-region traffic and error-rate normalizes.

On-call rotation and handoff template
- Rotation length: 7-day primary rotation with 24/7 coverage; daytime support window (08:00–20:00) has a shadow engineer for escalations.
- Handoff checklist (to be completed in Slack incident-handoff channel):
   1. Summary of unresolved alerts and current mitigations.
   2. Active runbook steps and next planned action.
   3. Links to traces, dashboards, and active bridge link.
   4. Contact list for SMEs and communications lead.
   5. Confirmation of when to page (escalation thresholds).

Game-day scenario catalog (examples)
- Scenario A: Multi-tenant latency regression caused by model rollout bug.
- Scenario B: Bulk KV cache eviction triggered by a rollback script.
- Scenario C: Spike in small short requests from a misbehaving customer integration causing autoscaler thrash.
- Scenario D: GPU host maintenance with incomplete draining resulting in transient OOMs.

Telemetry, SLOs and alert thresholds used in simulations
- Availability SLO: 99.95% (monthly) per-customer critical route. Error budget: 0.05% per month.
- Latency SLOs: P50 < 60ms, P95 < 180ms, P99 < 400ms for inference short-path.
- Alerts (examples):
   - High error-rate: service.error_rate > 1% for 5m -> PAGER (sev-1).
   - Latency regression: p95 > 500ms for 10m -> PAGER (sev-1).
   - Queue depth: queue.depth > 1000 -> PAGE (sev-2).
   - GPU util: avg GPU util > 90% for 10m and free mem < 8% -> PAGE (sev-1).
   - Circuit breaker hit: cb.open > 3 for 3m -> PAGE (sev-2).

Template: internal incident update (first 10 minutes)\\nSubject: [INCIDENT] {service} — {short-impact} — {region}\\nStatus: Investigating\\nSummary: We are investigating an elevated error-rate impacting {service} in {region}. Initial impact: {percent_customers} of requests affected; models impacted: {models}.\\nActions taken: 1) Opened bridge; 2) Throttled non-critical traffic; 3) Engaging SME.\\nNext update: {eta_minutes} minutes or upon material change.\\nOwner: {IC name}\\n\\nTemplate: customer-facing status (public)
- Title: Service disruption impacting {service} in {region}
- Body: We are aware of an issue affecting {service} that may cause elevated latency or failed requests for a subset of customers. We have identified the scope as {scope_summary} and are actively working on a mitigation. Estimated time to next update: {eta_minutes}. We will provide a full summary after recovery.

Postmortem minimum requirements (publish within 72 hours)
1) Executive summary (1–2 paragraphs)
2) Timeline of events (UTC timestamps)
3) Root cause analysis (3-level why)
4) Impact analysis (customers affected, SLOs breached, alerts fired)
5) Detection & response evaluation (what worked/failed)
6) Action items (owner, due date, verification criteria)
7) Runbook updates and test plan (what to exercise in next game-day)

Example postmortem action items
- Add route-specific circuit breaker tests to staging and include in weekly canary (owner: Priya Kapoor, due: 2028-03-01).
- Harden cache restore path with additional sanity checks and automated rollback (owner: Ethan Zhou, due: 2028-02-28).

Diagnostics and tooling quick reference
- Bridge creation: /opt/infra/bin/create-bridge --service {service} --incident {short-id}
- Quick logs query: sudo /opt/infra/bin/qlogs --service {svc} --minutes 30 --filter "error_rate>0.5"
- Runbook repository: confluence:/confluence/eng-sre/runbook-index

Proctoring and continuous improvement
- Proctors complete a scoring form and submit learning notes to the incident learning catalog after each lab. Scores drive a monthly skills heatmap used by SRE leads to schedule targeted mentorship.
- Every failed or partially successful scenario results in a follow-up small-group workshop within one week to rehearse corrected steps.

Appendix A — Example CLI snippets used in labs
- Check route latency:
  curl -s "https://metrics/api/query?metric=route_latency.p95&route=/generate&window=10m" | jq '.value'
- Apply a temporary throttle:
  curl -X POST https://admin/api/policies/throttle -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' -d '{"route":"/generate","rate":0.5,"ttl":600}'

Appendix B — Example customer message (post-recovery)
Thank you for your patience. We experienced a service disruption affecting {service} between {start} and {end}. Root cause: {short RCA}. Mitigations implemented: {list}. Next steps: {actions we will take}. If you were impacted please contact support@redwood.ai with subject line "Incident {id} impact".

Appendix C — Suggested rotation & certification policy
- All on-call engineers must complete the baseline simulator certification (score >= 80%) before rotating to primary on-call.
- Certification renewal: biannual.
